chapters.title: Conservation, gradients, and Fick's laws
chapters.question: What must a diffusion model conserve?
sections: Materials processes and the conserved amount
From a balance to Fick's second law
Directional diffusion and the tensor model
chapters.result: For fixed geometry with no reaction, partial_t c = -partial_x J; with J=-D partial_x c, partial_t c=partial_x(D partial_x c).
chapters.check: finite-volume conservation, layered-slab resistance, radial profiles, and rotated tensors

chapters.title: Laplace transforms and diffusion initial data
chapters.question: How do initial and boundary conditions select a solution?
chapters.result: Under stated regularity and convergence assumptions, D C_xx-s C=-c(x,0), where C is the one-sided time transform.
chapters.check: ODE residuals, initial data, inverse-transform coefficients, and transformed PDE units

chapters.title: Gaussian and error-function diffusion solutions
chapters.question: How does source geometry change the profile?
sections: Tutorial: inverse profiles without uncontrolled approximations
chapters.result: An instantaneous infinite-domain plane source of areal amount M has c=M exp(-x²/(4Dt))/sqrt(4 pi Dt).
chapters.check: normalization, second moment, error-function boundary limits, uptake and inverse-profile recovery

chapters.title: Finite domains and reproducible diffusion computation
chapters.question: How can analytic and numerical profiles check each other?
sections: Source Scilab demonstrations and Python counterparts
chapters.result: For the source-free constant-D uniform-grid explicit interior update, 0<=D dt/dx²<=1/2 makes each new cell value a convex average; positivity of the whole scheme also requires positivity-preserving boundary updates.
chapters.check: positivity, mass conservation, refinement against an exact solution

chapters.title: Crystal geometry, sublattices, and defect bookkeeping
chapters.question: Where can an atom move inside a crystal?
sections: Grain boundaries, misorientation and low-angle dislocation arrays
Ordered compounds, antisites and triple defects
chapters.result: A crystal defect count requires a specified sublattice and site multiplicity; equal defect numbers need not imply equal site fractions.
chapters.check: site counting, charge/stoichiometric balance, and geometry

chapters.title: Vacancy populations, binding, and defect measurements
chapters.question: How can equilibrium defect populations and binding be inferred from measurements?
sections: Vacancy formation free energy and entropy
chapters.result: Independent vacancy sites give x_v/(1-x_v)=exp(-g_f/(k_B T)); dilute favorable pair binding gives x_2v=(z/2)exp(g_b/(k_B T))x_1v² with explicit counting conventions.
chapters.check: free-energy minimum, missing-site balance, differential dilatometry and trapping-model identifiability

chapters.title: Random walks and atomistic diffusion mechanisms
chapters.question: How do discrete jumps produce a continuum coefficient?
sections: Continuum limit of a master equation
Tutorial: infer jumps from measured spreading
chapters.result: Independent isotropic jumps of length ell and total rate Gamma in d dimensions give D=Gamma ell²/(2d).
chapters.check: exact walk moments and seeded ensemble simulation

chapters.title: Correlation factors and tracer memory
chapters.question: Why is counting jumps insufficient?
sections: Vacancy-return memory and the finite-step correlation sum
Soluble persistent-walk model and conditional assumptions
Crystal self-diffusion factors and their limits
Binding, escape probability and parameter identification
chapters.result: For stationary zero-mean fixed-length jump increments with absolutely summable correlations, f=1+2 sum_{k>=1} E(step_0 dot step_k)/ell²; the finite-step factor includes weights 1-k/n.
chapters.check: one-dimensional persistent-walk exact moments

chapters.title: Temperature, pressure, and activation parameters
chapters.question: What does an Arrhenius slope actually measure?
sections: Tutorial: material-volume conventions and consistency checks
chapters.result: For a single Arrhenius mechanism with temperature-independent prefactor, d ln D/d(1/T)=-Q/R.
chapters.check: synthetic parameter recovery and two-path curvature

chapters.title: Free energy, interdiffusion, and phase formation
chapters.question: Which thermodynamic force drives composition change?
sections: Molar free energy and chemical potentials
New phases in a diffusion zone
chapters.result: For binary molar free energy g(N_B), mu_B-mu_A=dg/dN_B; a common tangent equates both component chemical potentials.
chapters.check: regular-solution curvature and tangent conditions

chapters.title: Reading composition profiles and diffusion paths
chapters.question: What can a diffusion-zone profile reveal?
sections: Tutorial: distinguish profile evidence from kinetics
chapters.result: A sharp locally equilibrated interface permits a concentration jump; conservation requires v(c_right-c_left)=J_right-J_left.
chapters.check: interface mass balance and scaling

chapters.title: Boltzmann–Matano analysis as an inverse problem
chapters.question: Can one profile determine composition-dependent diffusivity?
chapters.result: For an isothermal single-phase semi-infinite step with constant molar volume, no reaction or short-circuit heterogeneity and a strictly monotone smooth similarity profile, D(c*)=-[1/(2t c_x)] integral_{c_left}^{c*}(x-x_M)dc at interior nonzero-slope points; x_M is fixed by the mass-balance area condition.
chapters.check: recover a constant diffusivity and quantify noise sensitivity

chapters.title: Kirkendall markers, intrinsic fluxes, and Darken relations
chapters.question: Why can the crystal lattice move while a couple interdiffuses?
chapters.result: For constant V_m and binary intrinsic diffusivities, D-tilde=N_A D_B+N_B D_A; marker velocity v_K=V_m(D_B-D_A) partial_x c_B.
chapters.check: independent frame-transformation calculation

chapters.title: CALPHAD thermodynamics and kinetic databases
chapters.question: What information does a diffusion simulation need beyond a phase diagram?
chapters.result: Thermodynamic functions determine driving forces; mobilities determine rates, so equilibrium data alone do not identify diffusion time scales.
chapters.check: same equilibrium with distinct kinetic trajectories

chapters.title: Moving boundaries and multiphase simulation
chapters.question: How is interface motion coupled to diffusion?
chapters.result: For a quasi-steady layer with fixed concentration drop and partition jump, thickness squared grows linearly with time under stated sign and geometry conventions.
chapters.check: mass balance and an independent interface trajectory

chapters.title: Tracer profiles, SIMS, and electron-probe measurements
chapters.question: What does a measured depth profile identify?
sections: SIMS depth calibration and matrix effects
chapters.result: On the infinite line, a normalized Gaussian initial profile under constant-D diffusion has variance sigma_0²+2Dt; convolution with an independent centered Gaussian response adds its variance. A half-space surface source uses a different centered-variance convention.
chapters.check: recover D with and without instrumental broadening
chapters.tutorial_allocation: L40 radiotracer table/fit and depth-profile inverse examples; L40 mechanical/nuclear examples go to Ch17/18.

chapters.title: Mechanical relaxation and electrical diffusion probes
chapters.question: Which time and length scales does each probe observe?
sections: Tutorial: time ratios and parameter inference
chapters.result: For a single Debye relaxation, the loss peak occurs at omega tau=1; its activation fit uses ln omega versus 1/T_peak.
chapters.check: loss-peak sweep and independent Gorsky time ratios

chapters.title: NMR diffusion measurements and local jump times
chapters.question: Which time and length scales does each probe observe?
sections: Nuclear spin, resonance and relaxation conventions
Indirect T1 and T2 jump-time inference
chapters.result: For the stated free-diffusion pulsed-gradient sequence, echo attenuation is exp[-gamma² g² delta² D(Delta-delta/3)].
chapters.check: synthetic attenuation fit and timing/units sensitivity
chapters.source_allocation: L39 provides main NMR discussion; L40 relaxation tutorial; L41 opening recap provides NMR context only. Mössbauer and QENS are canonical Ch19.

chapters.title: Mössbauer and neutron scattering probes
chapters.question: Which time and length scales does each probe observe?
sections: Doppler energy shifts and linewidth conventions
Jump models and the low-q limit
chapters.result: Exponential free-diffusion self-correlation gives angular-frequency HWHM D q²; energy HWHM is hbar D q².
chapters.check: Fourier-transform linewidth and q-dependent jump model

chapters.title: Grain-boundary diffusion and kinetic regimes
chapters.question: When does a fast boundary dominate a measured profile?
sections: Boundary structure, segregation and transport area
Harrison A, B and C regimes
chapters.result: Boundary transport depends on both fast along-boundary diffusion and leakage into adjoining grains; the relevant bulk penetration scale is sqrt(Dt).
chapters.check: regime length-scale comparison and two-region conservation

chapters.title: Dislocation pipe diffusion and pathway competition
chapters.question: Can a tiny fast-path fraction control transport?
sections: Tutorial: compare lattice, boundary, and pipe routes
Designing an experiment to separate pathways
chapters.result: For parallel connected pathways sharing a gradient and local equilibrium, D_eff=sum_i phi_i D_i; this arithmetic average fails when exchange or connectivity is limiting.
chapters.check: path-volume sensitivity and series/parallel counterexample

chapters.title: Ordered, nanocrystalline, and quasicrystalline materials
chapters.question: How does structural order alter allowed transport mechanisms?
sections: Distinguishing structural evidence from rate claims
chapters.result: A larger interfacial volume fraction increases a simple parallel-path coefficient only if interfacial diffusivity, connectivity, and exchange assumptions remain fixed.
chapters.check: grain-size geometry and model sensitivity

chapters.title: Diffusion mechanisms in metallic alloys
chapters.question: How should diffusion rates across alloys be compared?
sections: Self diffusion, crystal classes and melting-point comparisons
Monovacancies, divacancies, anisotropy and phase transitions
Dilute solute binding and five-frequency transport
Historical electrostatic models and their failures
chapters.result: A measured diffusivity reflects pathway populations, jump mobilities, correlations and reference conditions; no single material label determines its ordering.
chapters.check: trap-limited transport, defect-population competition and controlled rate comparisons

chapters.title: High-entropy alloys and the evidence for diffusion claims
chapters.question: How should diffusion rates across alloys be compared?
sections: Composition, mixing entropy and phase identity
chapters.result: A diffusion ranking requires named species, phase, coefficient, temperature convention and comparable microstructure; high configurational entropy alone proves no universal kinetic ordering.
chapters.check: same-absolute versus homologous-temperature ranking and primary-data audit

chapters.title: Defect-mediated diffusion in semiconductors

sections: Dopant–defect pairs, dissociative and kick-out reactions
Retrograde solubility, oxygen and intrinsic gettering
chapters.result: The semiconductor diffusion coefficient depends on the populations and mobilities of participating defects; a single constant-D profile is a restricted process model.

chapters.title: Ionic solids, defect chemistry, and coupled charge transport
